name: Drum Bus Crack
description: The tallest drum hits shaved off on a bus, hard and quick, so the bus can come up without its peaks.

name: No Latency
description: For recording and playing in: once the rate, so it adds no latency, a soft edge a dB under full scale to catch what would clip.

name: Snare Tame
description: A snare's crack rounded by a diode pair's corner: its peak down six dB, its body left.

name: Tape Round
description: Tape's long, gentle approach to the ceiling over a broad knee: peaks rounded rather than cut, with a little density, and the output down to match.

name: Valve Warmth
description: A valve's lopsided curve, driven, half of it under what came in: even harmonics that thicken a bus or a bass.

name: Loud Master Front
description: A modern loud master's trick: a hard edge a dB under full scale, four dB into it, at sixteen times so the edge stays clean; the limiter after it then has little left to do.

name: Peaks Off the Master
description: Before Himlavalv on a master: two dB into a soft edge just under full scale, so the sharpest drum peaks are taken off here and the limiter after it works less and pumps less.

name: Transparent Edge
description: The gentlest clipping for a master: the sine curve, which comes to the ceiling flat, a broad knee, and sixteen times the rate, so next to nothing folds back.
